title: Expose recoverable native navigation failures without a second notification system

scope.subject: Turn YEIS camera-navigation failures into a visible persistent product notice with retry and dismiss while preserving the shared destination executor

research_summary: The shared destination executor already reports native YEIS camera failures through handleNavigationFailed, but the product clears the request and leaves only a root dataset plus console output. The pinned MIT YEIS UI already uses a single non-modal toast surface for transient feedback, while WAI-ARIA's alert pattern requires important dynamic messages to be announced without stealing focus and warns against disappearing too quickly. Mature Radix/React Aria toast products add queueing, focus hotkeys, swipe and provider machinery that is unnecessary for a single navigation failure. Reuse the existing YEIS notification concept, the current galaxy locate-caption visual language and React state: keep one persistent failure notice, preserve the exact failed camera request, allow a safe exact-target retry with a fresh requestId, and allow dismiss without changing destination identity.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS already exposes one non-modal showToast surface, supporting a small notification concept without importing the legacy UI wholesale.
ARIA alerts are for brief important dynamic messages, should not steal keyboard focus, and should not disappear so quickly that users miss them.

Radix Toast is a mature full notification component with provider, focus hotkey, swipe, queueing and foreground/background announcement semantics; that machinery is broader than this single exact-target recovery state.

React Aria provides a mature toast queue/accessibility subsystem, but adopting a new queue/provider is unnecessary when the product needs at most one navigation failure tied to the current camera request.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain pinned MIT YEIS as the full navigation product and reuse its single non-modal notification concept rather than adding another product shell.
No additional app framework is needed; accessibility requirements are satisfied by semantic HTML/ARIA in the current React surface.
Radix Toast and React Aria Toast are mature notification subsystems, but their queue/provider/focus/swipe machinery is globally disproportionate for one current navigation failure.
Existing React state/callback primitives plus the current caption styling close the exact gap with no new runtime dependency or authority.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS single non-modal notification semantics
candidates.reason: The notification concept fits the product, but legacy DOM/timing code and Turkish UI are not copied; Personal Universe owns the React presentation and persistent error behavior.

candidates.name: Radix Toast
candidates.reason: Excellent accessibility and interaction coverage, but adds provider/queue/focus/swipe machinery and a new dependency for a single current navigation failure.

candidates.name: React Aria Toast queue
candidates.reason: Mature accessible queue model, but a queue/provider is unnecessary while navigation exposes one authoritative in-flight/failed request at a time.

candidates.name: Existing React local failure/retry state
candidates.reason: Preserves the failed UniverseNavigationCameraRequest exactly, refreshes only requestId on retry, and renders one persistent alert using the existing UI vocabulary.

decision.rationale: Reuse the pinned YEIS single-notification concept and current React primitives. Keep one persistent, non-focus-stealing failure notice styled from the existing galaxy navigation caption. Retry reissues the exact failed camera request with a new requestId through the same YeisGalaxyScene path; dismiss only hides feedback. No new navigation, toast queue or router authority is introduced.
decision.fallback: If Personal Universe later accumulates multiple independent background notification sources, reassess Radix or React Aria as a single global notification subsystem rather than growing bespoke queues.
